title: AI Video Call Consultations: Ant Afu Surpasses 150 Million Users and Is Heading to Your Wrist

content_html:
Health management is shifting from "treating illness" to "preventing illness." According to a November 23 report from Fast Technology, at the 2026 Ant Afu Healthcare Ecosystem Conference recently held in Guangzhou, Ant CEO Han Xinyi offered two judgments: AI's most profound value for health is not curing disease, but helping people get sick less often and avoid serious illness; society pays a lot of attention to AI empowering medical care, but investment in AI promoting health is clearly insufficient.

More Than a Year Since Launch, the World's Largest AI Health App

There is no need for empty talk about market size—McKinsey estimates that if the factors affecting health are fully managed, global GDP could increase by an additional $16.4 trillion by 2050. Ant Afu has reached 150 million users in just over a year since launch, making it the world's largest AI health app. The most closely watched feature in the new version is real-time audio and video "Health Check" based on the Bailing healthcare large model: for minor problems, users can directly video call Afu, AI can make an initial remote observation and consultation, and real doctors can also be looped in to check. The "AI Health Manager" has also been upgraded, customizing blood sugar control, parenting, and weight-loss plans based on individual physical condition and goals; on the hardware side, AI health bands and rings have been launched, extending management scenarios from phones to wearable devices.

Three Changes, One Direction

Han Xinyi summed up the changes brought by AI into three points: First, the marginal cost of personalized services has been greatly reduced. Older people with chronic diseases can arrange their diet and exercise according to changes in blood pressure and blood sugar, and people trying to lose weight can have their plans dynamically adjusted according to body fat percentage. Second, smart hardware, test reports, and electronic medical records are integrated into a continuously updated health record, moving management from post-illness treatment to early warning of abnormalities. Third, AI connects in-hospital and out-of-hospital care, so patients still receive regular reminders and doctor consultations after discharge. All three point to the same thing: health is shifting from "the doctor's business" to "everyone's own business," making healthy living a daily routine that people can keep up every day.
